title: Microsoft Teams: more messages on screen in the iOS and Android apps
summary: The roadmap details and general Teams licensing and device requirements are supported. Hold because the page turns an undocumented rollback control into a definite claim that the service desk cannot revert the layout, and similarly asserts that no admin role is involved. Delivery through an app update is also not established.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether the new layout arrives automatically or requires a choice.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "568067" mobile default rollout; Teams "See more messages on mobile" licensing rollout default accessibility. Read roadmap, Microsoft Teams client and messaging policies; none states this layout's default.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific layout change.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "See more messages on mobile" licensing rollout default accessibility; Teams "568067" mobile default rollout. Read Microsoft Teams client, messaging policies, service description and system requirements; no feature-specific description found.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not say whether users can switch between layouts.
claims.quote: We are introducing a more streamlined messaging experience that displays more content on screen while improving readability when using Teams on mobile.

claims.claim: The roadmap does not specify whether chats, channels and meeting chats are all covered.
claims.quote: These updates make it easier to scan conversations and follow the discussion flow, helping users stay productive and engaged wherever they work.

claims.claim: Feature-specific rollout mechanics and an app version are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams "568067" mobile default rollout; Teams "See more messages" "update". Read roadmap and Microsoft Teams client; results describe general client servicing, not this feature's staging or app version.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not said how this layout treats device text-size settings.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile "See more messages" layout density default rollout 568067 licence text size; "Teams" "mobile" "new layout" "text size". Read system requirements and returned Teams app design excerpts; none describes this layout's text scaling.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; summary; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI or API control to select the old or new mobile message layout or set its density is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile message layout density admin policy PowerShell revert "568067". Read Manage messaging policies, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy syntax and searched layout/density/mobile, and Intune configure-teams-mobile; no matching control found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The licensing model is included within the supported Teams subscription entitlement for the mobile apps.
claims.quote: All supported subscription plans are eligible for access to the Teams web client, desktop clients, and mobile apps. Teams is available as part of qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings and as a standalone SKU.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate licence or add-on for this layout change.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "mobile" "message layout" "license"; Teams "See more messages on mobile" licensing rollout default accessibility. Read Teams service description and returned add-on/Premium licensing excerpts; none names this layout as an add-on.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes no meter for this feature.
claims.quote: We are introducing a more streamlined messaging experience that displays more content on screen while improving readability when using Teams on mobile.

claims.claim: Teams Android support is limited to the last four major Android versions.
claims.quote: Support is limited to the last four major versions of Android.

claims.claim: Teams iOS support is limited to the two most recent major iOS versions.
claims.quote: Support is limited to the two most recent major versions of iOS.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap describes a display change, with no change to message access or sharing described.
claims.quote: We are introducing a more streamlined messaging experience that displays more content on screen while improving readability when using Teams on mobile.

claims.claim: The roadmap mentions no sign-in, permission or device change and no effect on existing protection policies.
claims.quote: We are introducing a more streamlined messaging experience that displays more content on screen while improving readability when using Teams on mobile.

claims.claim: Intune app protection and Conditional Access policies exist for Teams on iOS and Android.
claims.quote: At a minimum, you'll want to deploy a Conditional Access policy that allows connectivity to Teams for iOS and Android from mobile devices and an Intune app protection policy that ensures the collaboration experience is protected.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/intune/app-management/configuration/configure-teams-mobile to sources for the existing mobile protection policies mentioned in Security & identity.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature performs no actions on its own.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "streamlined messaging experience" mobile update layout revert actions admin role. Read roadmap, Microsoft Teams client and messaging policies; no text establishes an absolute absence of autonomous actions for this feature.
claims.fix: Replace 'No change: the feature performs no actions on its own.' with 'No automated action is described in the roadmap item.' In the risk rationale, replace 'with no new data access, sharing or automated action' with 'with no new data access, sharing or automated action described'.

claims.claim: The service desk cannot revert the layout for a user.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile message layout density admin policy PowerShell revert "568067". Read messaging policies, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy and Intune configure-teams-mobile; no documented rollback found, but none states rollback is impossible.
claims.fix: Delete ', so the service desk cannot revert it for a user'. Keep only 'Microsoft Learn documents no admin setting to keep the current layout at the time of writing (November 2026).'

claims.claim: No admin role is involved in this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "streamlined messaging experience" mobile update layout revert actions admin role. Read roadmap, messaging policies and Microsoft Teams client; none states that no admin role is involved in this change.
claims.fix: Replace the Roles bullet with '**Roles:** no feature-specific configuration role is documented.'

claims.claim: The new layout comes with a Teams mobile app update.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "See more messages" "update"; "Teams" "streamlined messaging experience" mobile update layout revert actions admin role. Read roadmap and Microsoft Teams client; neither ties this layout's delivery to an app update.
claims.fix: Replace the service-desk bullet with 'Brief the service desk about the planned Teams mobile layout change and that no admin setting to revert it is documented at the time of writing.'

claims.claim: Messaging policies in the Teams admin center control which chat features users get.
claims.quote: Messaging policies are used to control which chat and channel messaging features are available to users (owners and members) in Microsoft Teams.

claims.claim: Immersive reader for messages is a messaging policy setting.
claims.quote: Immersive reader for messages - Turn this setting ON to let users view messages in Microsoft Immersive Reader.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy belongs to Teams PowerShell and updates messaging policies.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module. This cmdlet updates a Teams messaging policy. Custom policies can then be assigned to users using the Grant-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy cmdlet.

claims.claim: Teams messaging policy automation can control access to Immersive Reader for messages.
claims.quote: -AllowImmersiveReader: Determines whether a user is allowed to use Immersive Reader for reading conversation messages. Set this to TRUE to allow. Set this FALSE to prohibit.
